# v2.1.0 Implementation Verification

## Release Decision — 2026-11-17

The project owner explicitly authorized preparing and publishing **v2.1.0** after
the feature-branch test handoff. Release scope is the optional adapter packages,
configuration helper, adoption guide and maintainer evidence. Existing v2.0
projects need no mandatory migration; unchanged core rules and project templates
remain the compatibility boundary.

The owner accepted the reported Jira/Confluence read/write/update scope.
GitHub native hierarchy and Project updates were tested through the official
MCP server. GitLab reads/authentication were tested, with missing mutation
capabilities documented as workflow blockers. The release publishes adapters
that enforce these capability gates, not a guarantee of every target workflow.
Fresh-client prompt compliance, untested hierarchy/migration/deactivation paths
and edition/version limits remain explicitly documented in the evidence below.
No additional live customer writes are part of release preparation.

Final checks cover the ten local helper tests, changed Markdown links/anchors,
code fences, JSON/TOML evidence/examples, selective adoption/removal and unchanged
core files relative to v2.0.0. The approved feature source must be secured in the
upstream repository, merged through a pull request, and tagged on that exact
verified `main` commit. The GitHub release is the authoritative publication record.

Latest Atlassian evidence: [owner-reported Jira and Confluence verification, 2026-11-17](atlassian-verification-2026-11-17.md).
The owner accepted the tested read/write/update scope. V2 compatibility, native
Jira subtask writes, duplicate-free repeated setup, migration and deactivation
remain outside the supplied verification evidence. Earlier pending statements
below describe their historical checkpoints.

Latest GitHub live evidence: [GitHub Free acceptance, 2026-11-16](github-adapter-acceptance-2026-11-16.md).
It verifies basic native hierarchy and Project writes through the official MCP
server, with disposable targets removed afterward. Historical no-live-test
statements below describe the earlier implementation checkpoints; the linked
report records the newer results and their prompt/client-test limits.

## Feature-branch Test Handoff — 2026-11-16

The project owner authorized committing and pushing the current adapter revision
to `codex/feat/optional-integration-addons` for Jira and Confluence testing on a
separate customer machine. This authorizes source transfer for testing, not a
release, tag, deployment, customer-site connection, or remote content mutation.
Jira and Confluence runtime acceptance remains pending. Local helper tests,
Markdown checks and unchanged-core checks passed before this handoff.

## Local Scenario Walkthroughs

Disposable copies were used to apply the documented strategy manually with
illustrative local records. These are structural checks, not execution of an
installer, a live AI prompt, or a remote integration.

| Scenario | Evidence and result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh project | Copied optional instructions into a disposable setup with `docs/`; core entry/shared files, existing task ID, and sample completed content remained unchanged by copying. The normal bootstrap sequence was not altered or bypassed. |
| Existing project | Used a custom `knowledge/` root, completed overview/task, `TASK-010-007`, diagnostics default `on`, and a production-approval rule. Selective adoption retained those contents and settings. |
| Durable configured rules | Added an illustrative Jira record and a conditional pointer to it, without an `addons/` dependency. The record explicitly says no connector is authenticated and no writes are allowed. |
| Remove unused add-on | Removed the Confluence directory in the disposable copy and cleaned its index entry; selected guidance and project records remained available. |
| Remove all after setup | Removed the entire optional directory; the durable project record and its conditional pointer still resolved, and protected project documents and IDs remained unchanged. |
| No add-on selected | Core rules, roles, adapters, and templates are byte-for-byte unchanged in the actual diff; add-ons add no automatic activation, imports, or required bootstrap step. |
| Blocking and authorization gates | Text review confirms prompts resolve dependent decisions, inspect actual capabilities, and obtain only missing external-write authorization; selection alone grants no write permission. This is not proof of model compliance. |

## Runtime Limits and Publication Gate

No user account or target integration was configured. Authenticated Cloud/Data
Center/self-managed API behavior, connector permissions, rich-content rendering,
remote deduplication and concurrency, and live AI-client prompt behavior remain
unverified. The guidance explicitly requires those checks for each real setup.
No live compatibility claim or successful remote connection is made.

Before publication, the maintainer must review this evidence and its limits,
confirm authorization for Git/publication steps, and verify that the approved
source commit is secured in the upstream repository and used by the release tag.
Do not publish uncommitted working-tree contents or reuse v2.0.0 publication
authorization for this release.

## Deactivation Prompt Follow-up

All four add-ons now include a linked English `deactivation-prompt.md`. Static
review covers target-specific resource preservation, authorization reuse, shared
access, partial shutdown, verification, and recovery. Before shutdown, each prompt
requires comparing remote knowledge with local content and asking for content
migration, external retention, or exclusion decisions unless already explicitly
resolved. Required migration must be verified before access needed for it stops.
Prompts preserve provenance, stable IDs, existing documentation, and project data
rules, and report missing discovery access without claiming a complete handover.
These are instruction checks; no live migration or deactivation was performed.

## MCP Adapter Revision

The project owner clarified that these packages must be adapters with actual MCP
configuration, visible stable ID titles, and native ticket/task hierarchy. See
[the decision](v2.1.0-adapter-decision.md). This replaces the instruction-only
interpretation without changing v2.0 core workflow or project templates.

Delivered: shared and four product-specific MCP setup guides, executable
`addons/configure_mcp.py`, a pinned GitLab proxy example, updated prompts,
identity/hierarchy preflight, adapter state reporting, and shared-profile-aware
shutdown after required knowledge migration. Actual session catalogs and target
operation tests are required during project activation; a file preview is not
reported as a live connection.

Verification performed for this revision:

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/maintainers/tests -p 'test_configure_mcp.py' -v`: ten tests
  passed. They cover no-write previews, initial empty-tool discovery mode,
  no silent widening, existing content preservation, idempotency, conflicting
  profiles, Codex/Claude Code/VS Code formats, environment references, invalid
  inputs/configs, secret URL refusal, and symlinked destination refusal.
- Product guides and the shared contract were reviewed for native hierarchy,
  visible IDs, reciprocal read-back, partial results, and migration-before-shutdown.
- Local links/anchors/fences and the pinned proxy TOML example were checked.
- Core shared instructions, tool entry points, role profiles/adapters, and project
  templates remain unchanged from the committed source.
- Independent QA found a fresh-profile discovery gap; `--discovery-only` now
  emits an empty Codex allowlist. A reviewed manual merge promotes the allowlist
  after discovery. QA confirmed the fix and reported no remaining confirmed defects.
- Read-only review of the existing sandbox records confirms previously observed
  OAuth failure, working proxy authentication, flat issue creation, missing
  update/hierarchy operations, and rejected Quick Actions. These are historical
  sandbox results, not new live checks of this revision.
- Read-only metadata inspection confirms the existing local GitLab profile uses
  stdio and an explicit read-tool allowlist. Its package argument is not pinned;
  the new reusable example is pinned. The existing global profile and auth store
  were not changed or read for secret contents.

No authenticated MCP operation, remote ticket repair, native hierarchy mutation,
or live client reload was performed for this revision. Current GitLab operation
gaps remain blocked; local helper tests do not supply missing server features.
The revision is uncommitted until separately authorized for commit/push.

## Follow-up: Live Read and Fresh-project Prompt Tests

Actual Codex CLI0.164.0 calls exercised the GitLab integration prompt in initially
unconnected disposable projects, without importing a real GitLab MCP profile or
OAuth cache. The tested candidate was the uncommitted adapter revision. The
runner supplied non-secret target choices and explicit read-only scope.

- A denied-write/network run reported Prepared/Blocked honestly. A reviewed run
  wrote the discovery-only profile and reproduced native OAuth issuer failure.
- The pinned proxy path required normal registry resolution; offline pinned
  resolution failed despite package files being cached. Exact0.16.6 metadata and
  integrity were checked before proceeding.
- Fresh browser authorization was confirmed by the user. Initialization and a
  15-tool filtered catalog succeeded through the new independent auth store.
- The prompt-generated path lookup double-encoded a project namespace. Discovered
  numeric IDs worked; the adapter prompt/setup now explicitly prevents that error.
  Actual follow-up reads through the fresh profile verified all seven existing
  objects, ID titles, unchanged descriptions and preserved identities.
- The corrected exact prompt was called again from another unconnected fixture.
  Its diagnostic stopped at the human-action boundary; the operator kept a real
  callback alive, received user confirmation, and verified fresh reads. The shared
  guide now documents callback continuity rather than terminating on an auth URL.
- A separate fresh model session did not automatically expose the project profile
  with user configuration ignored. Explicit loading of only the generated profile
  succeeded: registered MCP version and issue-read calls completed. No automatic
  project-file loading or full model-policy compliance is claimed for that mode.
- Existing connection read-back and fresh browser inspection verify six native
  Tasks under their Spec parent, unique stable markers, unchanged content and
  checklists. Their prior UI repair is not a successful MCP hierarchy mutation.
- No remote content, title, type, parent, status, pipeline, or existing grant was
  changed by these checks. Secrets/auth caches and raw auth logs are not copied
  into this repository. Local helper tests remain ten passing tests.

Result: fresh connection and actual registered read access are verified under
these documented conditions. Native MCP update/type/parent mutations remain
unsupported in the observed catalog. Mutation/repeat-write/deactivation and
knowledge-migration acceptance are not passed by these read tests. Full adapter
write-workflow and release sign-off remain open.
